questions.question: You need to send traces, metrics, and logs from a Python FastAPI app to Application Insights by using OpenTelemetry. The solution must require the least amount of code. What should you do?

options.text: Install azure-monitor-opentelemetry and call configure_azure_monitor() at application startup
options.why: Correct. The Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro configures the SDK, the exporter, and the bundled instrumentations, including FastAPI, in one call.

options.text: Write each request to a Log Analytics table by using the Logs Ingestion API
options.why: This requires custom code for every request and does not create distributed traces.

options.text: Enable diagnostic settings on the App Service plan
options.why: Diagnostic settings export platform logs. They do not instrument application code.

options.text: Install the OpenTelemetry SDK and create a span manually in every route
options.why: This requires much more code than the distro, which instruments FastAPI automatically.

questions.explanation: The Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro sets up OpenTelemetry for Application Insights with automatic instrumentation for common libraries.

questions.question: A web API calls a retrieval service over HTTP. Both services are instrumented with OpenTelemetry. In Application Insights, the spans from both services appear in the same end-to-end transaction. What allows the spans to be correlated?

options.text: The trace ID, passed between the services in the W3C traceparent header
options.why: Correct. Context propagation sends the trace ID and parent span ID so that the receiving service continues the same trace.

options.text: Both services use the same cloud role name
options.why: The cloud role name identifies a service. Using the same name would merge them on the application map, not correlate requests.

options.text: Both services write to the same Log Analytics table
options.why: Sharing a table does not link individual operations together.

options.text: The span ID of the receiving service is copied to the calling service
options.why: Each service creates its own span IDs. The shared value is the trace ID.

questions.explanation: Every span in a trace shares one trace ID, propagated over HTTP in the traceparent header.

questions.scenario: A developer has obtained a tracer by calling tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__). The developer wants a custom span named retrieve-context, and any calls made inside the block must appear as child spans.
questions.question: Which code should the developer use?

options.text: with tracer.start_as_current_span("retrieve-context") as span:
options.why: Correct. This creates the span and makes it the current span, so spans created inside the block become its children.

options.text: span = tracer.start_span("retrieve-context") without making it current
options.why: The span is not set as current, so spans created inside the block are not parented to it.

options.text: trace.get_current_span().set_attribute("name", "retrieve-context")
options.why: This adds an attribute to an existing span. It does not create a new span.

options.text: logging.info("retrieve-context")
options.why: This writes a log record, not a span.

questions.explanation: start_as_current_span creates a span and sets it as the active context for the duration of the with block.

questions.question: Three Python services send telemetry to the same Application Insights resource by using the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro. On the application map, all three services appear as a single node. What should you configure so that each service appears as its own node?

options.text: Set a different service.name resource attribute, for example by using OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, in each service
options.why: Correct. The service.name resource attribute sets the cloud role name that the application map uses for nodes.

options.text: Set sampling_ratio to 1.0 in each service
options.why: Sampling controls how many traces are kept. It does not identify services.

options.text: Create a separate Log Analytics workspace for each service
options.why: Separate workspaces would split the data and make cross-service tracing harder.

options.text: Add a tenant.id attribute to every span
options.why: Span attributes add detail to operations. They do not set the cloud role name.

questions.explanation: Application Insights derives the cloud role name from the service.name (and optional service.namespace) resource attributes.

questions.question: Inside a custom span, a call to a model deployment raises an exception. You need the span to show the failure and the exception details in Application Insights. Which TWO actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Call span.record_exception() with the exception
options.why: Correct. This attaches the exception type, message, and stack trace to the span as an event.

options.text: Call span.set_status() with StatusCode.ERROR
options.why: Correct. This marks the span as failed so that it is reported as an unsuccessful operation.

options.text: Call span.set_attribute("sampled", False)
options.why: This only adds an attribute. It does not change sampling or record the failure.

options.text: Call configure_azure_monitor() again inside the except block
options.why: The distro is configured once at startup. Calling it again does not record the exception.

questions.explanation: record_exception captures the exception details, and set_status with an error code marks the span as failed.
